question: Is every animal afraid of man?
summary: Genesis 9:2, embedded in the post-flood Noachic covenant, has Yahweh place the fear and dread (morakem ve-hittekem) of human beings upon every beast of the earth, every bird of the sky, every creeping thing, and every fish of the sea — they are delivered into human hands. Proverbs 30:30 says the lion is strongest among beasts and turns away from no one. The Genesis text is a universal claim about every beast; Proverbs offers a counter-example that explicitly exempts at least one species.

reconcile.connective: Clarke reads the lion's dread as territorial avoidance — fleeing human settlements — rather than submission or retreat in a direct encounter.

discrepancy.connective: Christopher A. Baba's EvilBible.com — source of this exact question — sets Genesis's universal 'every beast' dread against Proverbs's fearless lion, which 'turneth not away for any.'

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley catalogues this exact pairing by name — "Man's fear and dread upon all beasts. Not upon the lion. Gen. ix. 2. Prov. xxx. 30" — and then resolves it: "The second passage, 'A lion which is strongest among beasts, and turneth not away for any,' may mean, 'for any beast' — another way of designating the lion as the 'king of beasts.' If, however, it implies, 'for any man,' the exceptional cases which this statement covers only prove the general rule that the presence of man intimidates all the lower animals."

link.title: Is there a Bible contradiction in Proverbs 30:30?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment of this exact verse pairing, citing Geisler & Howe's When Critics Ask (1992) for the same 'turns not away from other beasts' and 'exception proves the rule' arguments Haley gave in 1874.

excerpts.attribution: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832)
excerpts.excerpt_text: Tigers, wolves, lions, and hyenas, the determinate foes of man, incapable of being tamed or domesticated, flee, through the principle of terror, from the dwelling of man, and thus he is providentially safe.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly names the lion among the beasts whose Gen 9:2 fear-response is cashed out as avoidance ('flee...from the dwelling of man') rather than tameable submission — supplies the 'avoidance, not submission-in-encounter' distinction defenders use to square the lion's boldness in Proverbs 30:30 with Genesis's universal dread-grant.
excerpts.source_note_text: The fear of you and the dread, etc. - Prior to the fall, man ruled the inferior animals by love and kindness, for then gentleness and docility were their principal characteristics. After the fall, untractableness, with savage ferocity, prevailed among almost all orders of the brute creation; enmity to man seems particularly to prevail; and had not God in his mercy impressed their minds with the fear and terror of man, so that some submit to his will while others flee from his residence, the human race would long ere this have been totally destroyed by the beasts of the field. Did the horse know his own strength, and the weakness of the miserable wretch who unmercifully rides, drives, whips, goads, and oppresses him, would he not with one stroke of his hoof destroy his tyrant possessor? But while God hides these things from him he impresses his mind with the fear of his owner, so that either by cheerful or sullen submission he is trained up for, and employed in, the most useful and important purposes; and even willingly submits, when tortured for the sport and amusement of his more brutish oppressor. Tigers, wolves, lions, and hyenas, the determinate foes of man, incapable of being tamed or domesticated, flee, through the principle of terror, from the dwelling of man, and thus he is providentially safe. Hence, by fear and by dread man rules every beast of the earth, every fowl of the air, and every fish of the sea. How wise and gracious is this order of the Divine providence! and with what thankfulness should it be considered by every human being!
